articles.title: 'New kit' helps battle against bugs in Cornwall
articles.summary: The chemical-free decoys are used while clearing riverside vegetation.
articles.body:
Plastic dragonflies have been used as a decoy to deter biting insects.

Harrison Blake, Cromac Grounds Operative, said: "This is fast, fast becoming the most important piece of kit."

Blake and his co-worker Cian Davey use the chemical-free decoys while clearing riverside vegetation and say they work particularly well against horseflies.

Davey said: "Our dragonfly here keeps us safe and stops us getting eaten alive."

articles.title: Fã faz homenagens a Leandro e Cristiano Araújo no dia dos Finados | G1
articles.standfirst: Admiradores visitam túmulos dos artistas no Cemitério Jardim das Palmeiras e mantêm homenagens com flores e orações, em Goiânia.
articles.summary: Admiradores visitam túmulos dos artistas no Cemitério Jardim das Palmeiras e mantêm homenagens com flores e orações, em Goiânia.
articles.body:
O locutor e berranteiro Marcos Baixinho Reis é um dos admiradores que mantêm a tradição de visitar os túmulos dos cantores Leandro e Cristiano Araújo para prestar homenagens no Dia de Finados, celebrado nesta segunda-feira (2), no Cemitério Jardim das Palmeiras, em Goiânia . A saudade e a admiração pelos artistas fizeram com que ele cultivasse, ao longo dos anos, o hábito de tocar seu berrante no local.

“O berrante tem uma ligação com a maioria dos artistas da zona rural e do campo. Meu motivo de tocar o berrante é levar alegria com pensamento positivo”, afirmou.

Marcos contou que acompanha a dupla Leandro e Leonardo há 30 anos. Ele também relembrou que teve a oportunidade de tocar berrante para a mãe dos cantores, Dona Carmem, antes de ela falecer.

“Passo aqui para deixar uma rosa e rezar uma Ave Maria e um Pai Nosso pela alma dele e de toda a família. Peço ao Pai Eterno proteção e amparo para todos os familiares e fãs. Venho prestar essa homenagem e espero que os fãs tenham esse mesmo pensamento, porque nenhum de nós é para sempre”, destacou o locutor.

Fã toca berrante em túmulo de artistas em Goiânia — Foto: Ivan Duarte/TV Anhanguera

Outra admiradora que mantém a tradição é Silvânia Aparecida, de 65 anos. Fã da dupla Leandro e Leonardo desde o início da carreira, ela conta que visita o túmulo de Leandro todos os anos no Dia de Finados. A visita também é uma forma de homenagear o marido, que está sepultado no mesmo cemitério.

“Ele era uma pessoa muito, muito especial. Quando venho trazer uma florzinha para o meu marido, venho aqui no túmulo dele toda vez”, afirmou.

Silvânia disse que teve a oportunidade de assistir a um show da dupla uma vez. Mesmo com o passar dos anos, ela afirma que continua admirando os artistas e sentindo saudade.

Idosa visita túmulo do cantor Leandro, em Goiânia — Foto: Ivan Duarte/TV Anhanguera

Dia do Servidor e Finados: veja o que abre e o que fecha em Goiás

Os quatro cemitérios municipais de Goiânia, Santana, Parque, Jardim da Saudade e Vale da Paz, recebem, juntos, cerca de 100 mil visitantes por ano. Em 2026, a movimentação no Dia de Finados também foi intensa, com registro de filas no Parque Memorial.

Para receber a população, a Prefeitura de Goiânia intensificou os serviços de zeladoria nos cemitérios municipais. Além do reforço na limpeza, roçagem e conservação dos espaços, a Secretaria de Gestão de Negócios e Parcerias (Segenp) realizou melhorias na infraestrutura, como a modernização da iluminação e a instalação de câmeras de monitoramento.

A operação especial também incluiu a instalação de banheiros e bebedouros extras para os visitantes. Além disso, a Secretaria Municipal de Eficiência (Sefic) reforçou as equipes para orientar e fiscalizar a atuação de ambulantes; a Secretaria Municipal de Engenharia de Trânsito (SET) atua na organização e nos bloqueios de trânsito; a Secretaria Municipal de Inovação e Transformação Digital (SIT) auxilia os visitantes com informações sobre a localização dos túmulos; e a Guarda Civil Metropolitana (GCM) reforça o policiamento nos locais.

articles.title: Temporais com granizo ameaçam SC nesta segunda após estragos | G1
articles.standfirst: Instabilidade ganha força à tarde, principalmente em áreas próximas à divisa com o Paraná, segundo a Defesa Civil.
articles.summary: Instabilidade ganha força durante a tarde, principalmente nas áreas próximas à divisa com o Paraná.
articles.body:
Santa Catarina está sob alerta de novos temporais nesta segunda-feira (2), após registrar estragos no fim de semana . Segundo a Defesa Civil estadual, um sistema de baixa pressão favorece a formação de tempestades isoladas com raios, rajadas de vento e eventual queda de granizo à tarde.

A instabilidade, que segue um dia depois de imagens registrarem um morador retirando pedras de granizo com uma pá , em Fraiburgo , deve atingir com maior intensidade as regiões próximas à divisa com o Paraná, como Grande Oeste, Planalto Norte, Litoral Norte e o Vale do Itajaí.

O risco é de baixo a moderado para destelhamentos, queda de árvores, alagamentos e danos na rede elétrica.

🟡 Além do governo estadual, o Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia ( Inmet ) também emitiu um aviso de "perigo potencial" (alerta amarelo) para tempestades válido para todo o território catarinense até as 23h59 desta segunda-feira.

O órgão reforçou a chance de chuva e ventos intensos, além de queda de granizo.

Morador usa pá para tirar gelo após temporal de granizo em Fraiburgo (SC) — Foto: Reprodução/NSC TV

No domingo, um forte temporal com granizo e vendaval atingiu Fraiburgo. A tempestade danificou casas, comércios, escolas e o hospital da cidade, deixando 400 famílias atingidas. Na região, cerca de 59 mil imóveis ficaram sem energia elétrica.

Ninguém se feriu, e a prefeitura informou que atua nesta segunda para restabelecer os serviços afetados.

Morador usa pás para retirar gelo após temporal com granizo atingir hospital e 400 famílias em SC — Foto: Reprodução/NSC TV

Hospital de Fraiburgo atingido por temporal no domingo — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

Em caso de rajadas de vento, não se abrigue debaixo de árvores, pois há risco de queda e descargas elétricas e não estacione veículos próximos a torres de transmissão e placas de propaganda.

Evite usar aparelhos eletrônicos ligados à tomada.

articles.title: 'Como puderam autorizar?': deputada argentina questiona governo Milei sobre fuga de Flávio | G1
articles.standfirst: Marcela Pagano aponta possíveis irregularidades no controle migratório, na escolta policial e no uso de veículos diplomáticos durante a passagem do senador pela Argentina. Justiça do país determinou a preservação de imagens da fronteira e do aeroporto.
articles.summary: Marcela Pagano aponta possíveis irregularidades no controle migratório, na escolta policial e no uso de veículos diplomáticos durante a passagem do senador pela Argentina. Justiça do país determinou a preservação de imagens da fronteira e do aeroporto.
articles.body:
A deputada argentina Marcela Pagano cobrou explicações sobre a possível participação de autoridades do governo de Javier Milei na operação que permitiu a saída do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) do Brasil rumo aos Estados Unidos.

Em entrevista ao Fantástico, exibida neste domingo (1º), a parlamentar afirmou que testemunhos e imagens apontam possíveis irregularidades na passagem de Flávio e sua família pela Argentina, incluindo o uso de escolta policial e veículos diplomáticos.

"A irregularidade na passagem pelo controle de imigração argentino, a escolta de policiais e, depois, o transporte em carros diplomáticos do Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Argentina. São esses os elementos que eu apresento pra que a Justiça cobre explicações das autoridades argentinas sobre como puderam autorizar essa operação", afirmou a deputada.

A operação também passou a ser alvo de questionamentos na Justiça argentina, que determinou a preservação de imagens das câmeras de segurança da fronteira e do aeroporto de Puerto Iguazú, cidade vizinha a Foz do Iguaçu, no Paraná.

O Fantástico questionou o governo argentino sobre uma eventual colaboração na saída de Flávio do Brasil e na viagem do senador aos Estados Unidos.

O secretário de Comunicação da Presidência da Argentina, Fabian Fernandez, respondeu que o governo não tinha nada a declarar.

Registros migratórios e escolta policial

A reportagem do Fantástico teve acesso a documentos do sistema de imigração argentino que integram uma investigação realizada em cooperação internacional. Os registros revelam detalhes da operação montada para a saída de Flávio Bolsonaro do Brasil.

Segundo os documentos, duas vans da empresa Iguaçu Dallas Travel Turismo Ltda. cruzaram a fronteira de Foz do Iguaçu em direção à Argentina na noite de terça-feira (27).

Em uma delas, que havia saído de Cascavel, no oeste do Paraná, estavam registrados os dados da mulher de Flávio, Fernanda, e das duas filhas do casal.

O sistema também registrou três entradas de Flávio Bolsonaro na Argentina, na mesma van, em um intervalo de 34 minutos.

A primeira ocorreu às 22h37, com passaporte italiano. Três minutos depois, houve outro registro, desta vez com dados da carteira de identidade. Às 23h11, uma terceira entrada foi registrada com o passaporte brasileiro.

Os dois registros com documentos brasileiros foram posteriormente cancelados, permanecendo válido apenas o registro com o passaporte italiano.

A segunda van havia cruzado a fronteira cerca de sete minutos antes. Nela estavam registrados o motorista Neri Luiz Dala Corte, o advogado Roberto Jorge Alexandre, que já atuou na defesa do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, e o israelense Menachem Booky Halevy, apontado como ex-oficial do serviço de inteligência de Israel.

O jornalista argentino Nicolás Munafó, do canal de notícias C5N, estava no aeroporto de Puerto Iguazú quando as vans chegaram e relatou ao Fantástico ter visto uma comitiva acompanhada por veículos oficiais.

"Na frente, vamos dizer assim, da comitiva vinha uma caminhonete da Polícia de Segurança Aeroportuária, que é responsável pelos aeroportos da Argentina. Depois, vimos sair duas caminhonetes brasileiras, com placas do Brasil e motoristas brasileiros. E, em seguida, mais duas caminhonetes argentinas, uma delas com placa diplomática", contou.

A presença de uma escolta policial e de veículos com placas diplomáticas está entre os pontos questionados pela deputada Marcela Pagano, que também citou supostas irregularidades no controle migratório.

Segundo a parlamentar, os carros diplomáticos utilizados na operação seriam do Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Argentina. Ela cobra que a Justiça esclareça como as autoridades do país puderam autorizar a operação.

Como Flávio Bolsonaro chegou à Argentina?

Apesar de os documentos migratórios indicarem que Flávio entrou na Argentina por terra, fontes ouvidas pelo Fantástico afirmam que a principal linha de investigação aponta para uma chegada de avião.

Nessa versão, o senador teria deixado Brasília às 5h05 de terça-feira (27), em um jato ligado ao advogado Willer Tomaz, amigo de Flávio. A aeronave pousou às 8h40 em San Fernando, na região de Buenos Aires.

De lá, Flávio teria seguido em outro voo privado até Puerto Iguazú, onde, segundo a investigação, permaneceu por horas dentro do avião à espera da mulher e das filhas.

Investigadores também apuram relatos de funcionários do aeroporto que teriam visto o senador dentro da aeronave.

Já Fernanda e as duas filhas teriam deixado Brasília em outro avião, com destino a Cascavel. No aeroporto da cidade paranaense, embarcaram em uma van que seguiu até a fronteira com a Argentina.

O advogado Willer Tomaz negou, por meio de sua assessoria, que uma aeronave pertencente a ele ou a empresas vinculadas à sua família tenha sido utilizada por Flávio ou seus familiares para deixar o Brasil.

Após a chegada da família a Puerto Iguazú, Flávio, a mulher e as filhas seguiram para os Estados Unidos em um jato de luxo Gulfstream G400, operado pela empresa argentina Baires Fly.

O voo custou US$ 150 mil (cerca de R$ 800 mil), segundo o empresário Luis Grande, dono da companhia, em entrevista à agência France-Presse (AFP).

A aeronave fez uma escala em Guayaquil, no Equador, para reabastecimento, antes de seguir para Miami, nos Estados Unidos.

A família desembarcou na manhã de quarta-feira (28), no Aeroporto Executivo de Opa-Locka, na Flórida.

Flávio deixou o Brasil após o Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) determinar que ele entregasse seus passaportes à Polícia Federal.

O advogado Frederick Wassef, que representa o senador, afirmou ao Fantástico que nenhuma informação sobre a viagem é oficial ou foi confirmada. Ele também negou que a saída do país tenha sido uma fuga.

articles.title: Familiares reclamam de túmulos danificados e objetos roubados no Acre | G1
articles.standfirst: Visitantes relatam prejuízos com saques recorrentes em sepulturas e cobram mais segurança e conservação no Cemitério São João Batista. Prefeitura afirma que reforçou monitoramento.
articles.summary: Visitantes relatam prejuízos com saques recorrentes em sepulturas e cobram mais segurança e conservação no Cemitério São João Batista. Prefeitura afirma que reforçou monitoramento.
articles.body:
Visitar o túmulo de familiares no Cemitério São João Batista, em Rio Branco , nesta segunda-feira (2), tem sido motivo de tristeza e indignação para pessoas que encontram sepulturas danificadas e objetos furtados.

No local, considerado o mais antigo e um dos maiores da capital, familiares relatam prejuízos provocados por saques recorrentes, que atingem vasos, crucifixos, fotografias e outros itens deixados como forma de homenagem.

Aos 72 anos, Dilce Terezinha acompanha há décadas os túmulos do filho Tibério Gaspar Vogel, sepultado em 1997, e do marido Aniceto Vogel, que morreu em 2004. A família mantém uma manutenção mensal das sepulturas, mas, mesmo com os cuidados frequentes, já precisou lidar diversas vezes com os danos provocados por furtos.

Ela contou ao g1 que costuma visitar o espaço e acompanhar os reparos, mas se preocupa com as famílias que não conseguem ir ao cemitério com frequência e acabam encontrando os túmulos destruídos.

"Os nossos entes queridos foram, mas o sentimento fica. Por meio desse sentimento de gratidão com eles, a gente mantém vivo esse cuidado, esse carinho. A gente gostaria que as demais pessoas que são encarregadas da manutenção desses espaços também tenham um pouco de sentimento, porque quem está sepultado ali, cada um tem família", desabafou.

Aos 72 anos, Dilce Terezinha acompanha há décadas os túmulos do filho Tibério Gaspar Vogel, sepultado em 1997, e do marido Aniceto Vogel, que morreu em 2004 — Foto: Pâmela Celina/g1

A preocupação também é compartilhada por Raimunda El Shawwa, de 71 anos. A mãe dela está sepultada no São João Batista há 45 anos e o pai, há 13. Segundo ela, há dois anos, o túmulo dos pais foi saqueado pela segunda vez. Na ocasião, foram levados vasos de bronze e um crucifixo. Até as fotografias da família foram atingidas, com a estrutura onde ficavam expostas quebrada.

Raimunda afirmou que chegou a procurar a administração do cemitério, registrar boletim de ocorrência e pedir providências ao poder público, mas diz que os problemas continuaram.

"Eu venho aqui durante todo o ano, não é só no dia dedicado aos Finados. [...] A gente fica lutando e reorganizando os túmulos, que é um absurdo. Espero que a gente consiga, com muita luta, que já movimentei várias pessoas também que têm túmulos saqueados, para juntos reivindicarmos isso", relatou.

Raimunda El Shawwa, de 71 anos, visita a mãe dela que está sepultada no São João Batista há 45 anos e o pai, há 13 — Foto: Pâmela Celina/g1

Prefeitura afirma que reforçou segurança

A administração do Cemitério São João Batista reconhece a necessidade de melhorias na segurança. Francisca Silva, que trabalha há sete anos no local, afirma que houve reforço no monitoramento, com a instalação de nove câmeras, além da contratação de agentes para a portaria.

Segundo ela, a equipe administrativa também foi ampliada para auxiliar os visitantes na localização das sepulturas. Quem não sabe onde está enterrado um familiar pode procurar a administração, informar o nome da pessoa e receber a indicação da quadra e do lote.

"Deu uma melhorada em questão da segurança, a gente conseguiu colocar mais câmeras aqui, nove câmeras ao total. Sobre espaço, não tem mais, o cemitério já está bem lotado, quem já tem sua terrinha aqui consegue sepultar, fazer benfeitorias, mas não tem mais lote pra venda. Demos uma reforçada também com os agentes de portaria que foram colocados", disse.

Francisca Silva trabalha há sete anos no Cemitério São João Batista, em Rio Branco — Foto: Pâmela Celina/g1

O secretário municipal de Cuidados com a Cidade, Tony Roque, reforçou que a prefeitura também aumentou o número de vigias noturnos e melhorou a iluminação do cemitério. Ele reconheceu que os furtos ainda acontecem e disse que os casos são repassados às autoridades policiais.

O secretário acrescentou que a manutenção dos cemitérios é realizada durante todo o ano, e não apenas no período do Dia de Finados.

O Cemitério São João Batista funciona diariamente, inclusive aos fins de semana, das 7h às 17h. De acordo com Francisca, a administração permanece aberta durante o horário de almoço, com funcionários trabalhando em sistema de revezamento para atender quem procura informações sobre sepulturas.

articles.title: Mais de 53 milhões já votaram nos EUA, acima do total de 2022 | G1
articles.standfirst: Participação antecipada já supera o total registrado em 2022 e bate recordes em estados decisivos; Trump intensifica campanha na véspera do dia oficial da eleição.
articles.summary: Participação antecipada já supera o total registrado em 2022 e bate recordes em estados decisivos; Trump intensifica campanha na véspera do dia oficial da eleição.
articles.body:
Presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump. — Foto: Nathan Howard/Reuters

Mais de 53,6 milhões de americanos já votaram antecipadamente nas eleições de meio de mandato dos Estados Unidos , que acontecem nesta terça-feira (3). O número, divulgado neste domingo (1º) pelo Election Lab da Universidade da Flórida, já supera os cerca de 46 milhões de votos antecipados registrados em todo o processo eleitoral de 2022.

A votação antecipada presencial chegou ao fim neste domingo em estados como Nova York, encerrando uma etapa marcada por recordes de participação em diversas regiões do país . Os prazos variam entre os estados, e os votos enviados pelo correio ainda podem elevar o total nacional.

Dos votos registrados até o meio-dia de domingo, aproximadamente 29,8 milhões foram presenciais e 23,9 milhões foram enviados pelo correio.

A mobilização é especialmente expressiva em estados que concentram disputas competitivas pelo Senado. No Texas, mais de sete milhões de eleitores já haviam votado antecipadamente, enquanto a Geórgia e a Carolina do Norte também registraram forte participação.

O aumento do comparecimento ocorre em meio à impopularidade do presidente Donald Trump , que intensificou sua participação na campanha para tentar preservar a maioria republicana no Congresso. Embora não esteja na cédula, o presidente transformou as eleições em um teste para os dois primeiros anos de seu segundo mandato.

Em jogo estão todas as 435 cadeiras da Câmara dos Representantes, 35 vagas no Senado e diversos governos estaduais. O resultado determinará o equilíbrio de forças em Washington nos próximos dois anos.

Trump intensifica campanha e aposta na mobilização republicana O presidente intensificou sua participação na campanha neste fim de semana, com comícios em Iowa e Kansas, estados tradicionalmente republicanos onde as disputas pelo Senado ganharam atenção nacional.

Em Iowa, Trump discursou por mais de duas horas e pediu votos para Ashley Hinson, candidata republicana ao Senado, e Zach Lahn, que disputa o governo estadual.

O presidente também fez referência à vitória do time de futebol americano da Universidade de Iowa sobre Wisconsin, no sábado, para transmitir confiança sobre o resultado eleitoral.

“Mas vamos ter uma vitória muito maior na terça-feira”, afirmou Trump.

A estratégia não depende apenas de comícios presenciais. O presidente também aposta em uma maratona de comícios virtuais, os chamados tele-rallies, em que fala diretamente com eleitores por telefone.

Só nesta segunda-feira (2), véspera da eleição, estão previstos nove eventos desse tipo, entre o fim da manhã e a noite.

Trump também reservou um momento simbólico para a fase final da campanha. Às duas da tarde desta segunda-feira, no horário de Washington, o presidente tem um discurso previsto no espelho d’água em frente ao Memorial Lincoln, na capital americana.

Embora não esteja na cédula, Trump tem tratado essas eleições como uma disputa decisiva para a continuidade de sua agenda política e a manutenção do controle republicano do Congresso.

O otimismo mostrado nos discursos do presidente, entretanto, contrasta com os índices de aprovação de seu governo. Segundo pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos concluída em 26 de outubro, apenas 32% dos adultos americanos aprovam o desempenho de Trump, índice próximo do menor patamar registrado durante seu segundo mandato.

Entre os eleitores registrados, 47% declararam preferência por candidatos democratas ao Congresso, contra 36% que disseram apoiar os republicanos.

A economia é uma das principais preocupações do eleitorado. Segundo o mesmo levantamento, 73% dos entrevistados consideram que o custo de vida está caminhando na direção errada, em um contexto de inflação e aumento dos preços dos combustíveis após o início da guerra com o Irã.

A pesquisa também identificou maior entusiasmo entre os democratas para comparecer às urnas: 46% dos eleitores do partido disseram estar muito motivados para votar, contra 30% dos republicanos.

Michigan expõe divisão entre democratas e provoca ataques de Trump a candidato muçulmano Uma das maiores surpresas da reta final aconteceu em Michigan, estado que Trump venceu nas eleições presidenciais de 2024 e que agora concentra uma das disputas mais importantes pelo controle do Senado.

A deputada democrata Haley Stevens, derrotada nas primárias do partido por Abdul El-Sayed, anunciou neste domingo (1º) apoio ao republicano Mike Rogers, adversário de El-Sayed.

“Estou apoiando Mike Rogers para o Senado dos Estados Unidos ”, declarou Stevens em um vídeo publicado nas redes sociais, depois de participar de uma cerimônia religiosa ao lado do candidato republicano em Detroit.

A decisão representa uma ruptura incomum dentro do Partido Democrata a apenas dois dias da votação.

O conflito entre Stevens e El-Sayed está relacionado principalmente às divergências sobre Israel e a guerra em Gaza. El-Sayed, americano de origem egípcia e muçulmano, acusa Israel de cometer genocídio contra os palestinos e critica o financiamento militar americano ao país.

Stevens, por sua vez, condenou uma propaganda produzida por um grupo independente que associava o apoio dos Estados Unidos a Israel ao aumento do custo de vida. El-Sayed afirmou que não participou da produção do anúncio e que discordava de seu conteúdo.

A deputada também criticou a presença do comentarista político Hasan Piker em eventos de campanha de El-Sayed. A tensão levou a equipe do candidato democrata a retirar o convite para que Stevens participasse de atividades conjuntas nos últimos dias da campanha.

“Temos que defender nosso país. Não podemos apoiar o ódio. Não podemos apoiar Hasan Piker”, declarou Stevens ao justificar sua decisão.

O anúncio provocou uma reação imediata entre lideranças democratas. O presidente do Partido Democrata em Michigan, Curtis Hertel, acusou Stevens de abandonar os princípios que dizia defender. O líder democrata no Senado, Chuck Schumer, classificou o apoio ao republicano como uma traição.

El-Sayed procurou minimizar a controvérsia e direcionar a atenção para as propostas de sua campanha.

“No fim das contas, eu realmente não penso em Haley Stevens. Penso nos outros 9.999.998 habitantes de Michigan”, declarou o candidato, acrescentando que estava mais interessado nas políticas públicas do que nas disputas partidárias.

Trump, por outro lado, comemorou a decisão da deputada. O presidente a chamou de corajosa e afirmou que gostaria de vê-la no Partido Republicano.

Durante o comício em Iowa, também aproveitou para atacar El-Sayed, associando o candidato muçulmano a grupos extremistas.

“O que este país precisa é de um pouco de torta de maçã. Não precisamos dos comunistas, dos jihadistas, da Irmandade Muçulmana. Precisamos de torta de maçã”, declarou Trump, usando um símbolo tradicional da cultura americana para elogiar o republicano Mike Rogers.

O presidente também insinuou que, caso El-Sayed seja eleito, precisaria passar por detectores de metal para assumir sua cadeira no Senado. Trump não apresentou evidências de qualquer ligação do candidato democrata com organizações extremistas. As acusações foram denunciadas como racistas e islamofóbicas por lideranças democratas.

Michigan é estratégico para o controle do Senado. Os democratas tentam manter a cadeira atualmente ocupada por Gary Peters, que está se aposentando.

Se eleito, El-Sayed se tornará o primeiro senador muçulmano da história dos Estados Unidos .

Republicanos apostam em Trump; democratas tentam conquistar eleitores insatisfeitos A estratégia republicana às vésperas da eleição combina a mobilização da base conservadora com tentativas de conquistar eleitores independentes, especialmente por meio de discursos sobre imigração, segurança e economia.

O presidente do Comitê Nacional Republicano (RNC), Joe Gruters, destacou a participação de Trump e do vice-presidente JD Vance como parte dos esforços para ampliar o alcance eleitoral do partido. Em entrevista à Newsmax, Gruters também apontou a maior capacidade de financiamento das campanhas republicanas como um fator importante para a estratégia eleitoral.

Já os democratas procuram transformar a insatisfação com o governo em votos, concentrando suas mensagens no custo de vida, nas tarifas comerciais e nas políticas econômicas da Casa Branca .

Alguns candidatos, porém, adotaram uma estratégia diferente: evitar confrontos diretos com Trump e buscar aproximação com eleitores de diferentes orientações políticas.

É o caso de Rob Sand, candidato democrata ao governo de Iowa, estado que votou majoritariamente no republicano em 2024.

Sand critica a polarização política e descreve os dois grandes partidos americanos como clubes privados. Nos comícios, costuma perguntar quem é republicano e quem é democrata na plateia e convida os eleitores a cantar juntos “America the Beautiful”, uma música patriótica que também está entre as favoritas de Trump.

A estratégia procura apresentar uma alternativa ao confronto partidário tradicional, em um estado onde os democratas não conquistam uma eleição estadual de grande expressão há quase duas décadas.

Latinos e asiático-americanos podem alterar o equilíbrio eleitoral Outro fator acompanhado com atenção pelos dois partidos é o comportamento dos eleitores latinos e de origem asiática, comunidades que ampliaram apoio a Trump nas eleições presidenciais de 2024.

Dois anos depois, pesquisas indicam sinais de afastamento de parte desse eleitorado.

Segundo levantamento do Pew Research Center realizado entre o fim de setembro e o início de outubro, 51% dos eleitores latinos registrados preferem candidatos democratas à Câmara dos Representantes, contra 24% que apoiam os republicanos. Outros 18% ainda não haviam decidido em quem votar.

Entre os eleitores americanos de origem asiática entrevistados, 56% declararam preferência pelos democratas, contra 16% pelos republicanos.

A política migratória aparece entre os fatores de insatisfação. Segundo o Pew, 62% dos eleitores latinos registrados consideram que o governo Trump está indo longe demais nas deportações.

A avaliação, entretanto, está longe de ser unânime. Entre os latinos que apoiam candidatos republicanos ao Congresso, 47% consideram que o governo está adotando a intensidade adequada nas deportações, enquanto 33% defendem medidas ainda mais rigorosas.

O custo de vida também pesa sobre as escolhas eleitorais, especialmente diante do aumento dos preços dos combustíveis após o início da guerra com o Irã.

Os dados sugerem que a aproximação dessas comunidades com os republicanos em 2024 não representou necessariamente uma mudança permanente de alinhamento político. Também não significam que todos os eleitores insatisfeitos estejam migrando para os democratas: parte deles pode optar pela abstenção ou permanecer indecisa.

Em distritos onde as disputas são decididas por margens pequenas, mudanças na participação desses grupos podem ter impacto importante.

Mais do que uma disputa sobre a popularidade de Donald Trump , as eleições de terça-feira vão determinar se os republicanos conseguirão preservar o controle do Congresso ou se os democratas terão condições de ampliar a fiscalização sobre a Casa Branca e impor novos limites à agenda presidencial.

O resultado também oferecerá um primeiro retrato nacional da reação do eleitorado aos dois primeiros anos do segundo mandato de Trump.

articles.title: 20 pacotes de supermaconha são apreendidos no Norte do Piauí | G1
articles.standfirst: Polícia apurou que droga saiu da Zona Sul de Teresina rumo à Parnaíba.
articles.summary: A supermaconha apreendida no Piauí estava em um carro interceptado na PI-110, em Piracuruca, após monitoramento de carga avaliada em R$ 400 mil rumo a Parnaíba.
articles.body:
20 pacotes de supermaconha são apreendidos em Piracuruca — Foto: Reprodução

Dois homens, que não foram identificados pela polícia, foram presos suspeitos de tráfico de drogas e 20 pacotes de "supermaconha" foram apreendidos no domingo (1º), após uma abordagem policial na rodovia PI-110, na zona rural de Piracuruca, no Norte do Piauí.

A droga é avaliada em cerca de R$ 400 mil. Segundo a Secretaria de Segurança Pública estadual, a apreensão foi realizada após o monitoramento e levantamento de informações sobre o transporte da carga, que apontaram que a droga sairia da Zona Sul de Teresina rumo à Parnaíba .

Com a ajuda do trabalho de inteligência, os policiais interceptaram o carro e os suspeitos em Piracuruca. Durante a fiscalização, os policiais encontraram a droga no interior do automóvel e deram voz de prisão aos dois ocupantes.

Os suspeitos e o material apreendido foram encaminhados à sede do DENARC, em Teresina, para a realização dos procedimentos legais cabíveis.

*Eduarda Barradas, estagiária sob supervisão de Lucas Marreiros.

articles.title: Anchieta-Imigrantes tem lentidão na volta do feriado de Finados | G1
articles.standfirst: Operação Subida foi implantada no Sistema Anchieta-Imigrantes. O motivo é o excesso de veículos, em direção a São Paulo.
articles.summary: O trânsito na Anchieta-Imigrantes registra lentidão rumo a São Paulo, com a Operação Subida ativa para organizar o fluxo de mais de 340 mil veículos no feriado.
articles.body:
Movimento é intenso de motoristas que estão deixando a Baixada Santista — Foto: Reprodução/TV Tribuna

Os motoristas enfrentam lentidão nas rodovias do Sistema Anchieta-Imigrantes na volta do feriado prolongado de Finados, nesta segunda-feira (2). A Operação Subida foi implantada nas rodovias para atender a demanda em direção a capital paulista.

O Sistema Anchieta-Imigrantes registra pontos de lentidão nas rodovias dos Imigrantes, Anchieta e Cônego Domênico Rangoni ( veja os trechos abaixo ).

O motivo é o excesso de veículos, em direção a São Paulo. A estimativa da companhia era que cerca de 342 mil veículos passassem pelas rodovias de acesso à Baixada Santista até terça-feira (3).

A Operação Subida (2x8) foi implantada por volta das 11h. Neste caso, as duas pistas da Imigrantes e a pista Norte da Anchieta são utilizadas para a subida. A descida ocorre apenas pela pista Sul da Anchieta. Segundo a Ecovias, a Operação Subida pode durar até 1h e ser retomada das 6h às 14h nesta terça-feira (3), caso haja tráfego intenso.

Os demais trechos sob concessão apresentam boas condições. O tempo está encoberto no planalto, na serra e na interligação.

articles.title: Dia de Finados em Aracaju: Missas e homenagens marcam a data | G1
articles.standfirst: Visitantes levam flores, velas e fazem orações em memória dos entes queridos.
articles.summary: Dia de Finados em Aracaju conta com missas e homenagens nos cemitérios, onde vendedores de flores compartilham histórias de trabalho e saudade dos entes queridos.
articles.body:
Cemitério Cruz Vermelha em Aracaju. — Foto: Leonardo Barreto/ TV Sergipe

Familiares e amigos visitam os cemitérios de Aracaju nesta segunda-feira (2), Dia de Finados, para homenagear entes queridos. Orações, flores e velas são dedicadas à memória daqueles que já morreram.

Segundo o padre Flávio Roberto, da Paróquia Santa Rita de Cássia, a data é vista pela Igreja Católica como um dia santo. “É um dia para homenagear os que já se foram não apenas com saudade, mas lembrar que a vida continua após a morte”, declarou.

A Arquidiocese de Aracaju montou uma programação de missas realizada em diferentes cemitérios da capital durante o dia.

A tradição de homenagear quem já partiu também faz parte da rotina de quem trabalha com a venda de flores. Em meio à movimentação intensa de clientes nos cemitérios, esses trabalhadores encontram um momento para deixar o trabalho de lado e prestar suas próprias homenagens aos familiares e amigos que já se foram.

Suzan Kelly de Barros vende flores em Aracaju. — Foto: Leonardo Barreto/ TV Sergipe

A comerciante Suzan Kelly de Barros vende flores há 10 anos. No Dia de Finados, ela monta uma barraca em frente ao Cemitério da Cruz Vermelha, no Bairro Getúlio Vargas, na Zona Oeste de Aracaju. São cerca de 70 arranjos. Quando acabam, ela vai levar flores aos seus familiares que também estão sepultados neste cemitério.

“As pessoas vêm homenagear seus parentes e depois é a hora dos meus. Hoje é um dia de muita saudade para todos, seja para quem vem comprar ou para quem tá vendendo como eu”, disse Suzan.

Por outro lado, há quem prefira deixar as homenagens para outro dia. O comerciante Laelson Santos hoje se dedica apenas ao trabalho e escolhe outro momento para levar flores aos túmulos de seus familiares.

Laelson Santos- comerciante. — Foto: Leonardo Barreto/ TV Sergipe

“São 39 anos vendendo flores, há 11 estou aqui nesse cemitério. Além de priorizar as vendas, eu priorizo os outros que hoje têm mais tempo para homenagear seus parentes. A morte deixa uma saudade que não cura com os anos. Essa é uma forma de amenizar um pouco dessa dor”, falou.

Por trás de cada flor vendida, existem histórias, lembranças e sentimentos. No Dia de Finados, quem trabalha para manter viva a tradição de homenagear também entende que é o momento de recordar os seus próprios familiares.

Cemitério São benedito em Aracaju recebe visitas no Dia de Finados. — Foto: Anderson Barbosa/ TV Sergipe

Missa de Finados no Cemitério São Benetido em Aracaju. — Foto: Anderson Barbosa/ TV Sergipe

articles.title: US grand strategy falls short of delivering victory in Iran
articles.summary: In spite of glaring differences in capabilities of the US-Israeli combine vis-à-vis the Iranians, Operation Epic Fury has not led to a victory for the
articles.body: In spite of glaring differences in capabilities of the US-Israeli combine vis-à-vis the Iranians, Operation Epic Fury has not led to a victory for the Americans. Somewhere in their planning process, the strategic, political and economic aspects were not enmeshed adequately to arrive at the grand strategy required to achieve victory. A bleak situation has evolved, with Houthis re-entering the fray, and putting under the scanner Saudi Arabia’s military capabilities.An analysis of the US miscalculations leads to the conclusion, that much as the Americans have achieved militarily, they have not been able to impose their will on Iran. As the shortfalls are studied, it’s also essential to identify major dilemmas that await the Americans at the next turn.American miscalculations impeding evolving of grand strategyUnderestimating the Opponents Capabilities. The renowned military thinker Sun Tzu has stated, “If you know yourself but not the enemy, for every victory gained you will suffer a defeat.” Incorrect appreciation of the enemy capabilities can be the gravest of flaws in battle. The American assessment of Iranians resilience, especially the ability to absorb loss of top rung leaders, destruction of critical military and industrial capabilities, was flawed. They expected the Iranians to foldup once the decapitation campaign was successful. The resounding success in Venezuela, leading to capture of Maduro in January, 2026, possibly fanned euphoric deductions that proved untenable in Iran.The deduction that simultaneous with a successful decapitation campaign, the Iranians would rise up against an oppressive regime, proved wrong. Iran has a history that goes back thousands of years. It provides the nation a strong foundation and identity. These factors surface sharply to complement national cohesion when a nation is in danger. The US miscalculations are not new, though. When the US led coalition entered Baghdad, Iraq in April 2003, they expected a rousing reception that wasn’t quite there.Damage to Global Trade by Denial of Straits. The criticality of Strait of Hormuz was well known before the first American salvoes of missiles, aircraft, drones were released, however, did the Americans evaluate the force required to fully dominate the Hormuz with multi-layered Air Defence cover, physical occupation of its banks, disallowing Iranian minelaying endeavour, and also sustaining such deployment? Further, It doesn’t require sinking a super tanker to initiate a spike in freight costs. The insurance companies need barely an assessment of heightened risks to hike their rates.The possibility of Bab el Mandeb further choking global trade wasn’t perhaps fully factored into the costs of war. That the Houthis will resurface as a force in being, wasn’t possibly fully considered either.US Defence Pacts with Other Nations: The Myths. The US has its bases all over the West Asian region to create a defensive envelope that host countries had mostly taken as an impregnable shield. However, the Iranians have been able to penetrate the shield, fairly successfully. The US bases in the region include those at Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Oman, Saudi Arabia, Jordan. These bases have faced Iranian attacks. The faith nations had in the US to be possessing the will and capability to protect allies and partners has been substantially eroded.Disproportionate Costs of Sustaining War. The American economy has produced the world’s greatest military machine. They have run possibly the best intelligence-based operations that we have witnessed.The flip side of the coin is its cost that’s straining the world’s largest economy. When a USD 35,000-dollar UAV of the Iranians triggers the launch of a top end 2.1-million-dollar interceptor of the US Navy, the cost of the war pinches Admiral Brad Cooper, Commander of U.S. Central Command is on record stating that the Persian Gulf countries are split over their support to a war against Iran. These countries, having allowed the use of the bases to the Americans for striking Iran, invited waves of attacks from the Iranians. Under such circumstances it’s not strange for alliances being stressed, differences arising and well entrenched relationships feeling the tug.Geo Economics: The Tariff Battleground. With a tariff war running the course simultaneously, nations have begun to wonder, which way are geopolitical alliances headed. President Trump has literally opened an economic warfare battlefront against most of the world. The price of a gallon of petrol was already shooting up when his tariff follies hit across geographies for citizens to feel the pinch in procuring their daily bread and butter. Unfazed, the President has turned his guns on old friends like Canada, EU, Quad partner India and many more. In fact, the Canadian story promises to occupy considerable media space, soon. A ding-dong tariff battle is also being witnessed with Trump blowing the whistle for more tariffs today, and taking an U-turn, tomorrow.Road ahead: Issues meriting close calculationsAmerican Boots on Ground. As of now, there is no tenable reason to believe that the war will stop very soon. However, the US cannot afford to put boots on ground. The IRGC has displayed adequate tenacity already to deter Trump, hopefully. The US has ordered a heavy escalation for a major assault, post elections.Saudi Arabia has High Stakes. They are the biggest oil exporters and also one of the top importers of weapons, globally. They should be able to take the fight to the Houthis. Reliance on air power alone will not do, and the Mecca agreement will take time to be productive!The World Order. It may witness changes, notwithstanding the results of November, 2026 elections in the US, or the post Trump era. Some old geopolitical alignments are already on crutches, while new ones are developing shoots. Bipolarity is mostly anticipated. The Chinese Prime Minister Xi Jinping said during his recent visit to the US, “ Achieving the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and making America Great Again, can go hand in hand.”Russian Decline. Though being often referred to as a declining power, Russia has displayed its ability to stall NATO spreading further East, The expansion of NATO at this stage, needs to be reviewed in-house, keeping in view its triggering an escalation in Ukraine.Most of the world is looking for peace in Iran, Gaza and Lebanon to start with, and deescalation in other conflict-ridden areas. The Iran War is also a loud warning to great powers not to underestimate the middle powers, or even well-armed militias with State backing. They may not be able to tilt the scales decisively, but the can certainly increase the costs disproportionately.

articles.title: North Shields mother told to make appointment to give birth to baby who had died
articles.summary: Newcastle Hospitals NHS Trust apologises for care it says "fell short of the standards" expected.
articles.body:
Warning: This article contains themes and images some readers may find upsetting.

A seven-month pregnant woman whose unborn baby died after she was discharged from hospital while suffering from a life-threatening condition was told by staff to make an appointment to give birth.

Danielle Brown, 31, from North Tyneside, said she was devastated to have to return home knowing the baby she was carrying was no longer alive.

She said no family should be put through the same experience and wants hospitals to offer alternatives for those grieving.

After she was discharged from hospital suffering with pre-eclampsia, Danielle insisted on returning to the maternity unit as she felt so unwell and was seen by doctors.

She was told her daughter had died but, instead of delivering the baby, the hospital sent her home and told her to ring to book a slot to give birth.

Her partner Anthony Miller, 34, described it as "horrible... lying in bed and holding that belly" knowing their baby was not alive.

The Newcastle Hospitals NHS Trust said it fully accepted "aspects of the care we provided fell short" and offered a "heartfelt apology".

Danielle and Anthony had been delighted to learn they were having a baby girl, who they decided to call Maisie.

"I was just over the moon, I couldn't be happier," Anthony said.

But in February 2023, seven months into her pregnancy, Danielle woke up feeling unwell.

Her face was swollen, as were her hands and feet - all potential signs of pre-eclampsia , which can be life threatening to both mother and baby.

The couple went to the Northumbria Specialist Emergency Care Hospital in Cramlington, Northumberland, but medics found problems with Maisie's heart rate and told Danielle her baby needed to be delivered immediately via emergency caesarean section .

"Maisie's heart rate had dropped and a midwife ran in and said 'don't panic, but I need to pull the emergency cord - you're having your baby'," Danielle said.

The midwife told her space was being found for her at the Royal Victoria Infirmary (RVI) in Newcastle and doctors there "were going to do the section", she said.

She was transferred by ambulance but, once in Newcastle, Danielle did not have the operation and was instead put on a ward.

"A consultant came to see me and he said I am staying in hospital until Maisie was born," she said.

But, the following day, another doctor reviewed her and sent her home.

Within 24 hours, again feeling unwell, Danielle called the maternity unit and said she was told she probably had a stomach bug. But she insisted on being seen.

"When I finally had a scan, the screen was turned away and there was no sound," Danielle said. She remembers turning to her partner and saying: "I think she's gone."

Doctors were unable to find Maisie's heartbeat and they told Danielle her baby had died.

But instead of delivering the baby, as she expected, Danielle was given a phone number, and sent home. She said they told her to "give us a call on Friday morning, and book a slot to come in and have Maisie".

"It was horrible," Anthony said. "Lying in bed and holding that belly, and still being able to feel Maisie but knowing she wasn't alive."

Two days later, after 10 hours in labour, Danielle gave birth.

"When Maisie was born the room was silent," she said. "Seeing Maisie was bittersweet. She was perfect. I told her she was beautiful and I loved her.

"It was devastating that my first experience of holding a baby was holding my stillborn daughter."

Speaking publicly for the first time about what happened, Danielle said no-one should be sent home still carrying a baby who has died.

"Don't," she said. "Just take that family and help them. Help them.

"When we left hospital, we gave Maisie one last cuddle and kiss and told her we loved her and were sorry things couldn't have been different."

After saying goodbye to their daughter, the couple faced further distress. To leave the hospital they had to walk past other parents holding their babies.

"We should have been leaving with our baby too, but we were leaving with a memory box," Danielle said.

"All the new mums were walking out carrying their babies. That will stay with me forever."

The couple want every hospital in the UK to provide an alternative way out for grieving mothers, to "make a different route for a parent who has just lost a child".

The trust's executive director of nursing and midwifery, Ian Joy, said: "We fully accept that aspects of the care we provided fell short of the standards the family had every right to expect and offer a heartfelt apology for this.

"Following a detailed review in 2023, we improved urgent assessment for women who come to our maternity services with unexpected symptoms or suspected complications and introduced quicker escalation procedures when there are concerns."

Legal executive Faisal Ali, from the law firm Irwin Mitchell, said pre‑eclampsia could be life‑threatening without appropriate care.

"What happened to Danielle and Maisie vividly highlights the human cost of care failings," he said.

"The trust admitted Danielle should not have been discharged on either the 14th or 15th of February 2023. Had she remained in hospital, monitoring would have shown the need to speed up delivery and Maisie would have been born alive."

An NHS England spokesperson said: "These failings in care are unacceptable and should never have happened.

"Anyone experiencing the loss of a baby should be fully supported by a specialist maternity team so they can make choices about their care that are right for them."

articles.title: 'Severe' deterrent call after Jersey Airport drone disruption
articles.summary: Islanders say the disruption to flights caused has been concerning and "ridiculous".
articles.body:
People have called for deterrents to be "severe" to prevent drones being flown illegally near Jersey Airport, which has led to disrupted and diverted flights.

Flights were affected on Friday and Saturday evenings after unauthorised drone activity was reported, leading to services being cancelled or diverted to other airports, including Paris.

Islanders said the disruption caused had been ridiculous and were worried it could happen again unless the perpetrators were "frightened" from doing so.

The island's government said the situation was being treated extremely seriously and anyone with information about the drones or their pilots should contact States of Jersey Police.

A police spokesperson said the drone activity was reported in active flight paths at the airport.

Flying drones within Jersey Airport's restricted airspace zone without prior permission from Air Traffic Control is illegal.

Under the Air Navigation (Jersey) Law 2014 , anyone who is deemed to have endangered the safety of an aircraft could be fined or imprisoned for five years.

Islander Stuart Abraham said he hoped the incident would not be copied by others and he hoped authorities were "very serious" about preventing it happening again.

"Something needs to be written into the law which really frightens drone pilots off to prevent them doing it in the first place," Abraham said.

"I'm not talking about bringing back the birch, but certainly if they were threatened with automatic imprisonment or something like that, it might work."

Another resident, Jonathan Hudson, said the whole situation had been quite concerning.

He added: "I don't understand why they're doing it, it's all unnecessary.

"Because of the last two nights with all the cancellations and disturbance, something's got to be done.

"I don't understand why these people aren't getting caught."

Sue Dawes, who said her son lived near the airport, said she was worried a similar incident could lead to a "terrible accident".

"What are they [the drone pilots] thinking?" Dawes said.

"They know it's going to cause a lot of havoc and distress for a lot of people, especially those trying to get away for medical reasons or trying to come home."

Senator Lyndon Farnham, Jersey's Chief Minister, said people should be "under no illusion" about the seriousness of the incidents.

"Operating a drone close to an airport is not a prank or a harmless hobby," he said.

"It puts public safety at risk, disrupts critical transport infrastructure and can have significant consequences for hundreds of travellers and businesses.

"To those responsible, the message is clear - if you are identified, you should expect to face the full consequences of the law."

articles.title: Hebron governor says Israeli forces withdraw from city after 10-day siege
articles.summary: Hebron Mayor Youssef al-Jaabari says families forced from their homes can return and students can go to school.
articles.body:
The governor of Hebron says Israeli forces have withdrawn from the city in the southern occupied West Bank after a 10-day siege, allowing displaced families to return home.

“Palestinian security forces have taken full control of the area following the Israeli withdrawal,” Governor Khaled Dudin announced on Monday.

“Relevant authorities and Palestinian security forces are monitoring developments on the ground and working to provide the necessary conditions for residents to return safely,” he said.

The Israeli military imposed a siege on Hebron on October 23 after a shooting attack near the city allegedly by two Palestinians that killed two Israeli soldiers and wounded three others. Israeli forces later killed the two suspects.

Hebron Mayor Youssef al-Jaabari told Al Jazeera the municipality was officially informed of the withdrawal at 6am (04:00 GMT).

“For the first time in 10 days, schoolchildren are going to their schools; university students are now on their way to their universities,” he said, adding that five universities had been closed during the siege.

“There was a complete closure, no entry or exit from the city, and all aspects of life, whether economic, educational, health, or even those related to municipal work, had completely stopped.”

Al Jazeera’s Mohamad Atrash, reporting from Hebron, said vehicles carrying displaced families began arriving minutes after the withdrawal, with residents congratulating one another on returning safely.

In one residential building used as a military post, Atrash found damaged furniture, ransacked rooms and food left behind by soldiers.

Residents of the building told Al Jazeera they had been forced out of their homes at 2am, with Israeli troops giving them five minutes to gather any medicine, phones or personal documents.

Families had been told the displacement would last one to three days, Atrash said. Instead, it stretched to 10, and some returning residents said money and personal belongings had been taken from their homes.

The Palestinian Civil Defence urged residents not to touch suspicious objects or enter damaged buildings before they had been inspected, the official Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.

Atrash said Israel’s military initially said the Hebron operation would target the homes of the two suspects in the killing of Israeli soldiers, but later widened the scope of the operation to the entire governorate, home to about 800,000 people, closing its checkpoints and seizing homes in al-Jalda and Ein Deir Bahha as military posts. Some 537 families were forced out at night and had to take shelter with relatives elsewhere in the city.

More than 3,300 Palestinians were displaced or otherwise affected, according to the Hebron governorate.

The Hebron municipality said on Sunday that Israeli forces had demolished 15 homes and structures and that 327 shops had closed, with direct economic losses exceeding 12 million shekels ($3.8m) a day, Wafa reported.

“Everything damaged we will rebuild,” Mayor al-Jaabari said, as municipal crews headed to al-Jalda, Ein Deir Bahha and Shubat al-Malh to assess damage.

About 80,000 students in the city were unable to attend school, according to Wafa. Atrash said some 262,000 students across the governorate missed nine days of classes.

Hebron, the occupied West Bank’s main economic centre, contains 220 of the Palestinian territory’s 940 Israeli military checkpoints and gates, Atrash said, adding that the closures disrupted 4,000 factories.

Mohamed Helles, an expert on Israeli affairs, said the operation was launched days before Israel’s general elections last month and was partly “an attempt to harvest electoral points at the ballot box” for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his right-wing allies.

Netanyahu’s electoral bloc secured the most seats but failed to win a majority in the vote, leaving Israel without a clear path to a new government.

articles.title: Bangladesh garment factories disrupted as protests continue for third day
articles.summary: Workers in Bangladesh’s largest export sector are demanding a minimum wage increase amid rising inflation.
articles.body:
Hundreds of garment factories in Bangladesh are facing disruptions as worker protests over low pay and the rising cost of living rock the country’s industrial hubs.

There was a heavy police presence in the Mirpur industrial area of Dhaka on Monday and reports of protests taking place for the third day in the Savar, Ashulia and Gazipur areas, Al Jazeera’a Tanvir Chowdhury reported from the capital.

About 500 factories were temporarily shuttered after the protests began on Saturday. Thousands of workers have taken to the streets, facing tear gas and sound grenades from police.

In an attempt to quell the demonstrations, Bangladesh formed a new wage board on Sunday to review the minimum wage for garment workers. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, meanwhile, held an emergency meeting with his ministers and advisers.

Workers are seeking a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka ($242), more than double the current wage of 12,500 taka ($101).

Bangladesh’s garment industry is worth about $38bn and is a key source of export earnings and employment.

But workers’ current wages are “not enough because of the rising cost of living”, Chowdhury said.

Workers “cannot handle the lifestyle with that kind of money, and they want a share” of the multibillion-dollar export industry, he added.

The protests come as Bangladesh’s garment industry, which competes with Vietnam’s, Cambodia’s and India’s, faces a range of challenges.

Factory owners said the industry is struggling with higher costs, energy market uncertainty during the United States-Israel war on Iran and slowing demand in some export areas.

Still, Bangladesh has “among the lowest garment wages in the world”, said Babul Akhter, general secretary of the Bangladesh Garment and Industrial Workers Federation and a representative for workers on the wage board.

“If factory owners cannot pay workers properly, they should negotiate better prices with international buyers. They cannot build a business on the backs of underpaid workers,” Akhter added.

The president of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association, Mahmud Hasan Khan, said the government “has already taken a step by forming the wage board”.

“We expect workers to allow the review process to proceed,” he said.

If protests continue throughout Monday, Khan added, “we will have no option but to invoke the ‘no work, no pay’ provision.”

articles.title: Craig Silvey: Australian author sentenced to prison over child exploitation offences
articles.summary: The author of Jasper Jones and Runt pleaded guilty in May after police raided his home months earlier.
articles.body:
Australian children's author Craig Silvey has been sentenced to seven months in jail for possessing and distributing child exploitation material.

In handing down her sentence, Judge Hayley Cormann called Silvey's actions "repulsive" and "degrading".

In January, Silvey was arrested after police raided his home in Western Australia and seized several electronic devices. In May, the 44-year-old pleaded guilty to possessing and distributing child exploitation material and in October he was jailed pending his sentencing.

The father-of-three is best known for his award-winning young adult novel Jasper Jones and children's book Runt, both of which were later made into movies.

"You have devastated and betrayed the trust of thousands of people, and you've let entire communities down," Cormann said on Monday, according to WA Today.

Police said Silvey had online chats, in which he discussed child exploitation, open at the moment they turned up to raid his house.

In them, the court heard, Silvey had described himself as "extremely open minded" and "obsessed with taboos".

He'd discussed his sexual interest in children as young as five with another user of a pornography site, and detectives found images and videos of other adults abusing children on his devices.

He was initially charged with four offences, but prosecutors later dropped two.

Prosecutors said Silvey contributed to the "cycle of abuse" victimising the children in the images, and argued a harsh sentence was required.

However, the author's defence lawyer said he did not have a "sexual interest in children" and was seeking out "the most depraved material" as a form of "emotional" self harm.

"His behaviour provided temporary relief from psychological agitation," Eloise Barker said.

She said Silvey had displayed genuine remorse for his offending, and that his high profile and the resulting media scrutiny - which lead to his former partner and children relocating interstate - was already a form of punishment.

Judge Cormann did not accept many of her arguments, and said Silvey's offending was extremely serious.

"These children, the victims of this type of offending, are real and are traumatised… the consequences for them from these abuses are long lasting and very, very traumatic," she said, according to The Australian.

Silvey was sentenced to seven months in jail, backdated to 22 October. He is eligible for parole.

Silvey's coming-of-age novel Jasper Jones sold more than half a million copies and was awarded the Book of the Year Award by the nation's peak publishing body in 2010.

The novel, set in Western Australia with two teenage boys as the main characters, was also shortlisted for the International Dublin Literary Awards and the Miles Franklin Literary Award.

It was later turned into a film starring Toni Collette and Hugo Weaving in 2017 as well as a stage play.

Another of his acclaimed works is 2022's Runt, about the adventures of an 11-year-old girl and her stray dog and set in the Australia outback. It was also adapted for film in 2024, featuring Celeste Barber.

Since his arrest, publishers and book shops have pulled his works from shelves while schools in some states have removed Jasper's books from teaching lists.

articles.title: Bulgaria elects pro-Russia president Iliana Iotova in runoff, defeats pro-Western rival
articles.summary: Bulgaria's president Iliana Iotova, who supports diplomatic engagement with Moscow and opposes military assistance to Ukraine, has won the presidential
articles.body: Bulgaria's president Iliana Iotova, who supports diplomatic engagement with Moscow and opposes military assistance to Ukraine, has won the presidential runoff held on Sunday, securing a decisive lead over her pro-western rival Andrey Gyurov.The largely ceremonial presidential contest saw Iotova, an ally of prime minister Rumen Radev, face Gyurov, a banker and former caretaker prime minister backed by the pro-Western opposition.According to estimates released by several polling agencies, Iotova secured between 57.4% and 58.2% of the votes, comfortably ahead of Gyurov, who received between 38.6% and 39.6%.Celebrating her victory alongside Radev, Iotova said her campaign had centred on "incomes, peace and the challenges that lie ahead".European commission president Ursula von der Leyen congratulated Iotova on her win. In a message on X, she said she looked forward to continuing cooperation with Bulgaria on issues ranging from security and defence to competitiveness and energy independence.Black Sea tensions dominate election backdropThe election took place amid growing security concerns following a series of drone attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea. Several ships were hit off Bulgaria's coast in October, leaving 21 people missing. The incidents are believed to be linked to the wider fallout from the Russia-Ukraine war.Although Radev has said the attacks appeared to benefit Russian interests and summoned Moscow's ambassador, his government maintains that there is currently no evidence directly connecting Russia to the incidents.Following Iotova's victory, Radev said Bulgarians had chosen "the future over the past", adding that they had voted for normalcy and a stable, clear direction for the country.Iotova set to become Bulgaria's first elected woman presidentIotova, 62, assumed the presidency earlier this year after Radev resigned to contest parliamentary elections. Sunday's victory will make her Bulgaria's first directly elected woman president.A former journalist and European parliament member, she was elected vice-president alongside Radev in 2016 and 2021. She supports Bulgaria's membership of the European union and NATO but maintains that a resolution to the Ukraine conflict can be achieved only through negotiations.After casting her vote in Sofia, Iotova said she wanted Bulgaria to be strong within a strong Europe while retaining sovereignty over its decisions.Gyurov, 50, a former deputy governor of the Bulgarian National Bank, accepted the election outcome and stressed the need for national unity."We have laid a solid foundation upon which we can build," he told reporters, while describing his preferred vision as one of a secure, stable and European Bulgaria.Low voter turnout highlights political divisionsBulgaria's close historical ties with Russia continue to divide public opinion over the country's approach to Moscow.Sociologist Boryana Dimitrova of the Alpha research institute said concerns about war had played a significant role in the campaign, adding that Iotova had presented herself as the "president of peace". She also described the election as crucial for Radev and his allies in maintaining political stability.The first round of voting, in which Iotova narrowly finished ahead of Gyurov, recorded a historically low turnout of 23%. Participation in Sunday's runoff was projected to be around 27%.Petar Doitchinov, a 67-year-old retired engineer, said he had skipped the first round because he expected the contest to go to a runoff. He eventually voted for what he called "the lesser evil", explaining that neither candidate fully reflected his understanding of democracy.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 'Always been anti-Hindu': Mumbai mayor's jibe at Dia Mirza after BMC removes Diwali campaign video; actor responds
articles.summary: MUMBAI: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has removed actor Dia Mirza’s video from its pollution-free Diwali campaign after Mumbai BJP chief
articles.body: MUMBAI: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has removed actor Dia Mirza’s video from its pollution-free Diwali campaign after Mumbai BJP chief Ameet Satam objected to her inclusion, triggering a political row, with Mayor Ritu Tawde calling the actor “anti-Hindu” and saying she had been blacklisted.Mirza, who had appealed to citizens to avoid bursting firecrackers and celebrate an environment-friendly Diwali, questioned the criticism of a campaign based on public interest and the Bombay High Court’s directives.Speaking to ANI, she said, “Why should anyone be critical of a video that the Honourable Bombay High Court and BMC have made me record in public interest? Air Pollution is an area of concern and all efforts to reduce pollution should be welcomed because its a matter of public health.”The BMC had launched the campaign amid rising air pollution in Mumbai, urging citizens to celebrate Diwali in an environment-friendly manner in line with a Bombay High Court directive.Several celebrities were roped in to spread the message, including Mirza, actors Madhuri Dixit and Nishigandha Wad, and cricketer Ajinkya Rahane.However, Mirza’s clip was removed from the civic body’s social media pages on Sunday after Satam objected to her inclusion in a post on X, tagging the BMC’s official account.“We don't need lessons on how to celebrate #Diwali from @deespeak. Our traditions are deeply rooted in our culture,” Satam wrote.Within hours of his post, the BMC, led by Municipal Commissioner Ashwini Bhide, removed Mirza’s video.Campaign videos featuring Madhuri Dixit, Nishigandha Wad and Ajinkya Rahane continued to remain on the civic body’s X and Instagram pages.Dia Mirza reacts after BMC removes Diwali campaign videoReacting to the controversy, Mirza said in a social media post, “Koi paise nahi liye hain. Bhalai ka zamana hee nahi raha (I did not charge (BMC) any fee (for the Diwali campaign). There is no goodness left in this era).”The BMC’s post accompanying her video had stated that, in accordance with the High Court’s directives, bursting firecrackers on public roads, lanes and footpaths was strictly prohibited.Mayor Ritu Tawde defended the removal of the video and made remarks against the actor on Monday. “Dia Mirza has always sided with divisive forces. She had trolled PM Modi on the NEET exam issue,” Tawde told reporters.“She has always been anti-Hindu. We have blacklisted her,” the mayor added.Opposition questions BMC's decisionOpposition leaders criticised the civic body for taking down Mirza’s clip, questioning whether the administration had acted under political pressure.Shiv Sena (UBT) spokesperson and former Mumbai mayor Kishori Pednekar asked whether the civic administration had “become a slave of the BJP or its Mumbai president”.Alleging that Satam’s interference in the civic body’s day-to-day functioning was increasing, Pednekar said the administration should not have succumbed to what she termed the BJP leader’s “communal agenda”.MNS corporator Yashwant Killedar also criticised Satam, saying that if the BJP Mumbai president was so fond of firecrackers, party office-bearers should burst as many crackers as they wished outside his residence.“Our Diwali can be celebrated even by lighting a single lamp and a lantern. Does the BJP approve of Satam's brand of 'hypocritical Hindutva' that supports bursting firecrackers in the name of religion?” he asked.Nitesh Rane questions Dia Mirza's stand on other religious festivalsBJP minister Nitesh Rane also criticised Mirza, questioning why she had spoken about pollution during Diwali but had not offered similar advice during other religious festivals.“Dia Mirza tweeted about Diwali, but she never tweets or offers such advice during Eid, Muharram or Bakri Eid,” he said.“People like her are against the Sanatan Hindu religion. I will discuss this issue with CM Fadnavis and focus on preventing such matters in the future,” Rane added.Shiv Sena spokesperson Shaina NC, meanwhile, said Mirza should know the significance of Diwali and the need to be mindful of pollution.“Dia Mirza, whose name itself means light, should know that the Festival of Lights refers to Diwali. Everyone knows the need to be mindful of pollution and avoid bursting firecrackers,” she said.Union minister Ramdas Athawale said the issue should not be linked to any particular community, while underlining the right of every religion to celebrate its festivals.“Dia Mirza belongs to the Muslim community, but this is not a matter of any particular community. In India, the Constitution given by Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar grants every religion the right to celebrate its festivals,” he said.“Just as Muslims celebrate Eid and observe Ramadan, members of the Hindu community also participate in these celebrations. If firecrackers are not burst, Diwali may lose some of its significance. However, we must also be concerned about excessive pollution,” Athawale added.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Halloween turns deadly across US as gun violence leaves at least 24 dead, 94 injured
articles.summary: More than two dozen people were killed and nearly 100 injured in a wave of violent shootings across the United States over Halloween weekend.
articles.body: More than two dozen people were killed and nearly 100 injured in a wave of violent shootings across the United States over Halloween weekend.The violence stretched from California to Delaware, with several shootings reported near university campuses and in nightlife districts. In Dallas, three separate shootings in the Deep Ellum neighbourhood left at least four people dead and 15 injured. In Birmingham, Alabama, gunfire outside Legion Field after the annual Magic City Classic left one person dead and eight others wounded.The weekend’s violence also included a shooting at a Spirit Halloween store in Fairfield, California, where a pregnant woman was killed and six others were injured. In Delaware, two mass shootings within just over an hour left one person dead and several others wounded, including at an outdoor party in Ellendale and along Main Street near the University of Delaware.“This is not normal,” Delaware governor Matt Meyer said in a statement after the shootings. “We must never accept gun violence as a part of life in Delaware.”CNN’s preliminary estimate put the toll at at least 13 people killed and 92 injured, based partly on figures compiled by the Gun Violence Archive. A later report by the New York Times put the number at at least 24 dead and 94 wounded across the country. The figures reflect different preliminary tallies of a fast-moving series of incidents.Shootings disrupt Halloween celebrationsOne of the first deadly incidents occurred on Friday night at a Spirit Halloween store in Fairfield, northeast of San Francisco. Police said gunfire broke out at around 8.30pm, killing a 31-year-old pregnant woman. Six others were wounded, three critically. The shopping centre subsequently cancelled a planned trick-or-treating event.In Flint, Michigan, a woman was killed and three people, two teenage boys and a man, were injured in a shooting at a party shortly after midnight on Saturday, WJRT reported. In Wichita, Kansas, four people were shot at an after-party early Saturday, including a 36-year-old man who was struck in the face by a stray bullet while looking out of his window, KAKE reported.In Birmingham, two shootings occurred minutes apart after the Magic City Classic, the annual football game between historically Black universities. Police said one person was killed and eight others were wounded in gunfire near vendors outside Legion Field shortly before 8pm on Saturday.A 17-year-old who was not affiliated with either university was taken into custody, mayor Randall Woodfin said. The teenager had a firearm fitted with a Glock conversion switch, he added.Gunfire near college campuses and party venuesDelaware reported two mass shootings in just over an hour on Saturday night. State police said a gunman fired into an outdoor party in Ellendale shortly before 10pm, striking nine people. A 17-year-old girl later died of her injuries; those wounded ranged in age from 17 to 22.At around 11.13pm, six people were shot along a crowded Main Street near the University of Delaware in Newark, police said. All were taken to hospitals.Near Edinburg, Texas, seven people were wounded at a Halloween birthday party shortly before midnight, according to the Hidalgo County Sheriff’s Office. All suffered non-life-threatening injuries, KRGV reported.Two cities named Bloomington, one in Illinois and the other in Indiana, also reported shootings early Sunday. In Bloomington, Illinois, police found multiple people with gunshot wounds on a residential street near Illinois Wesleyan University. A 19-year-old woman was pronounced dead at the scene, while seven others were injured, including a woman in critical condition.In Bloomington, Indiana, seven people aged between 17 and 27 were injured when gunfire broke out near a large crowd in the downtown area, WISH reported. Police detained a person who fled the scene with a firearm, but said they had not established whether that person had fired it.In Fayetteville, Arkansas, six people were shot, all six were taken to hospitals with non-life-threatening injuries, police said.Nightlife districts see deadly shootingsIn Jackson, Mississippi, two people were killed and four others injured in a shooting at a nightclub hosting a costume party early Sunday, police said. WAPT reported that two masked men entered the club and at least one opened fire on the dance floor.Dallas recorded three shootings in its Deep Ellum nightlife district within about 75 minutes, beginning shortly after midnight. At least four people were killed and 15 others injured, police said.In Jacksonville, Florida, two separate shootings at Halloween parties left two people dead and 11 injured. A 17-year-old girl was killed while waiting in line for a party at around 1.45am, with two others wounded. Just over two hours later, gunfire at a house party left a 20-year-old man dead and nine others injured, the Jacksonville Sheriff’s Office said. Police said both incidents followed fights that escalated into gunfire.The violence was not confined to party venues. In Detroit, a five-year-old girl was shot in the chest while playing in the back room of her home after trick-or-treating. The child was in stable condition.Halloween and the risk of violenceThe shootings came just over two weeks after a gunman killed three students and a teacher in a special-needs classroom at an elementary school in Oregon.Halloween is among the most violent days of the year, according to an analysis cited by NYT of FBI incident data from Boston between 2005 and 2009 by Northeastern University criminologist James Alan Fox. In that analysis, October 31 ranked third for violent incidents, behind only July 4 and January 1. Fox said it was the most dangerous day of the year for minors.Experts say the combination of large gatherings, alcohol consumption, drug use and access to firearms can heighten the risk of violence. But preventing shootings across bars, streets, parking lots and private parties remains difficult.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
